question: John Crowley, who wrote Engine Summer, may not enjoy the same fame as the most widely read American authors of the past fifty years, yet his writing has attracted several powerful advocates, among them the poet James Merrill and the literary critic Harold Bloom. Journalist Graeme Wood reports that Bloom claimed to have reread Crowley's novel Little, Big no fewer than forty-six times; in an afterword published after his death for a 2022 edition of the book, Bloom called Crowley a "major writer" and declared, "There is no other book by a writer still with us that I love as deeply." Based on the text, which statement would both Harold Bloom and James Merrill most likely endorse?
option a: John Crowley is not an American writer.
option b: John Crowley's novel Little, Big does not deserve to be widely read.
option c: John Crowley's novel Little, Big should be read at least forty-six times.
option d: John Crowley is a very good writer.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Bloom's praise and Merrill's championing of Crowley both signal that they regard him as an excellent writer.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
Approximate Numbers of Speakers of Four Native Languages
Language | Region | Number of speakers
Hopi | Southwest | 6,080
Tlingit | Alaska Panhandle | 1,240
Zuni | Southwest | 9,620
Mohawk | Northeast | 1,950
According to a 2015 report by the US Census Bureau, the Southwest's Zuni language ranks among the most commonly spoken Native languages in what is today the continental United States, claiming roughly 9,620 speakers. Hopi, another Southwest language, is spoken by fewer people than Zuni, yet its speaker population still numbers in the thousands. Per the Census Bureau report, the number of Hopi speakers in the US is approximately ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The table lists Hopi with 6,080 speakers, a figure in the thousands but fewer than Zuni's 9,620.

question: Which quotation from a student best illustrates the underlined claim? Museums occasionally put portions of their holdings on the internet. Both Vienna's Albertina Museum in Austria and Lima's Museo de Arte de Lima in Peru have posted digital images of some of their works in online collections. Online collections make it far easier for people to encounter art held by museums that are not located near them.
option a: "The last time I went to a museum, I spent the whole day looking at different things on display."
option b: "The Albertina Museum is far away from where I live, but I was able to look at some of its art online today."
option c: "I probably won't visit the Albertina Museum because I don't like art museums very much."
option d: "My family members enjoy going to museums when they travel."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: This student viewed art from a distant museum online, directly illustrating that online collections ease access.

question:
Which choice most logically completes the text?
Antonia Olivia Dolan and colleagues asked musicians and nonmusicians, all with clinically average hearing, to listen to recordings of nature sounds and of music in popular styles such as classic rock and heavy metal, adjusting the volume until their listening enjoyment was greatest. For any given recording that a musician and a nonmusician each named as their favorite among those in the study, the researchers found that the ideal volume tended to be higher for the musician than for the nonmusician. Thus, if a musician and a nonmusician both chose Led Zeppelin's "Whole Lotta Love" as their favorite recording and the musician preferred to hear it at 90.2 decibels, the nonmusician would be expected to ______
option a: prefer listening to other music at 90.2 decibels over listening to "Whole Lotta Love" at that volume.
option b: find listening to "Whole Lotta Love" at 90.2 decibels less enjoyable than listening to it at a lower volume.
option c: not find it enjoyable to listen to any recordings at a volume as low as 90.2 decibels.
option d: enjoy listening to the nature sounds at 90.2 decibels more than listening to "Whole Lotta Love" at 90.2 decibels.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Since the nonmusician's optimal volume is lower, they would enjoy the song more at a volume below 90.2 decibels.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Pablo Picasso is celebrated for overturning the conventions of traditional painting: in his cubist canvases he broke objects and figures into fragments so that several viewpoints appear at once, refusing to let his expression be constrained. Less widely recognized is that Picasso--who once complained that the writers of his era had "limited themselves to moving around words somewhat while respecting the syntax"--also composed poetry that flouted standard grammar, semantic relationships, and text structure. The paintings and the poems are therefore connected in that ______
option a: the poems are intended to be understood as explanations of the artistic inclinations reflected in the paintings.
option b: both types of work are characterized by the simultaneous representation of multiple points of view that Picasso is known for.
option c: the poems present many of the same subjects as the paintings but with different thematic approaches.
option d: both exhibit Picasso's prioritization of creative expression over the standard rules of the art forms.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: In both his paintings and his poems, Picasso placed free creative expression ahead of each form's conventional rules.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Silvia Moreno-Garcia is now known chiefly as a novelist, thanks in part to the success of her 2020 horror novel Mexican Gothic, but she began as a highly productive writer of short fiction. Before her breakout year in ______ Moreno-Garcia had already placed more than 75 short stories in a range of literary outlets, including "The Moon Is Shattered" (2008) in Byzarium, "Jaguar Woman" (2009) in Shimmer, and "Collect Call" (2012) in Expanded Horizons.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma after the introductory prepositional phrase correctly sets it off from the main clause.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Working as an archaeologist, Dr. Rubén G. ______ investigates historical sites throughout the US Southwest and Mesoamerica, a region that takes in ancient Maya locations such as Arroyo de Piedra in Guatemala.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation belongs between the subject "Dr. Rubén G. Mendoza" and its verb "investigates."

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Within a chemical equation, the quantity known as molar mass is useful for converting between the mass of the reactants and the mass of the product. The liquid ______ have molar masses of 156.31 and 46.07 g/mol, respectively.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The naming of the two compounds is essential to the sentence, so no commas should separate it.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Elvis Presley's iconic Blue Rain jumpsuit was set with blue rhinestones. Historians note that decorations like these could add between twenty-five and fifty pounds to each of Elvis's stage outfits. ______ the fabric used for the outfits was light and flexible, allowing him freedom of movement.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The contrast between the heavy adornments and the light fabric calls for "On the other hand."

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Charles Demuth's 1931 painting Chimney and Water Tower is a quintessential Precisionist work. The Precisionists aimed for a cold, machine-like perfection, using crisp lines, geometric shapes, and smooth, brushstroke-free surfaces. ______ Precisionist works frequently depict skyscrapers, bridges, and factories, drawing attention to the engineered symmetry of these angular structures.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The subjects follow logically from the Precisionist aims, so "Accordingly" fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? A research team headed by the Portuguese scientist Isabel C.F.R. Ferreira found that many species of mushrooms contain chemicals called phenolic compounds, such as cinnamic acid and catechin. ______ Ferreira detected cinnamic acid in Agaricus blazei mushrooms and catechin in Lentinus edodes mushrooms.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The specific mushrooms illustrate the general claim, so "For example" is appropriate.

question:
The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two bird species. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
The Galápagos petrel is a bird species found in the Galápagos Islands, and it weighs 425 grams on average. The small tree finch is also a bird species found in the Galápagos Islands, and it weighs 13 grams on average.
option a: The small tree finch and the Galápagos petrel can be found in the Galápagos Islands.
option b: The small tree finch and the Galápagos petrel are both bird species.
option c: On average, the Galápagos petrel weighs 425 grams, while the small tree finch weighs only 13 grams.
option d: The Galápagos petrel is a bird with an average weight of 425 grams.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Contrasting the two average weights directly emphasizes a difference between the species.

question:
The student wants to present the study's research methods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Suzanne K. Birner headed a study that examined rocks on the seafloor to better understand the history of Earth's mantle. The team gathered rock samples from two seafloor ridges. They determined the samples' period of formation (the Archean eon) and their oxidation level (extremely low). The high temperatures of the Archean likely caused the rocks' low oxidation. Birner's group proposes that, contrary to earlier theories, the oxidation of Earth's mantle has stayed stable over time. The results help explain the unusual conditions that allowed life to develop on Earth.
option a: By studying these ancient rocks, the team aimed to challenge previous theories about changes in Earth's mantle over time.
option b: To further analyze the origins of Earth's unique conditions, researchers focused on rocks from the Archean eon, when Earth's temperatures were extremely high.
option c: Birner's team analyzed the age and oxidation levels of rock samples collected from two seafloor ridges.
option d: Birner led a study to better understand the history of Earth's mantle and explain the conditions that allowed life to develop.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Describing the sampling and the analysis of age and oxidation presents the study's actual research methods.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Some social scientists contend that although a belief in the importance of individual autonomy is essential to democracy, the public's grasp of economics is also central to its later understanding of a state's politics, and that if an electorate is to function, economic questions cannot be left to experts alone. Economics is too ______ to leave to economists alone.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The passage stresses how much is at stake in economics for the electorate, so "critical" fits best.

question:

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Silvia Moreno-Garcia is best known as a novelist, partly because of the success of her 2020 horror novel Mexican Gothic, yet she launched her career as a prolific short story writer. The list of more than 75 short ______ she published before Mexican Gothic includes works such as "Ahuizotl" (2015) and "Water" (2007).
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The essential relative clause introduced by "that" takes no comma before it.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? On a 2022 expedition led by research zoologist Andrea Quattrini, scientists discovered a new species of black coral off the coast of Puerto Rico. Like other black corals, the newly discovered species, which they named Aphanipathes puertoricoensis, has coiled branching structures that ______ it survive in the deep sea.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The plural subject "structures" requires the plural verb "help."

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Enormous plumes of dust from the Sahara Desert that drift across the Atlantic Ocean can affect tropical cyclones in intricate and contradictory ways. On one hand, the dust can promote the formation of ice clouds in the cyclone's core, increasing precipitation. ______ the dust can lower sea surface temperatures around the cyclone's core, weakening the storm.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The two opposing effects set up by "On one hand" are completed by "On the other hand."

question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text? Ruth Asawa was a versatile artist who worked across many forms, notably her distinctive tied-wire sculptures, but making art was not her only commitment. She also wanted to bring art to the children of her hometown, San Francisco, California. To that end, she cofounded the Alvarado School Arts Workshop in 1968, which brought artworks and artists into public schools, and in 1982 she helped establish a San Francisco public arts high school that was later named after her.
option a: Asawa's unique sculptures were appreciated more by local art communities than they were nationwide.
option b: Asawa inspired many other artists to share their work with students in public schools.
option c: Asawa's interest in art education prompted her to create art programs for students in San Francisco.
option d: Asawa left a promising career as a sculptor to work as an art teacher in San Francisco schools.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text centers on how Asawa's commitment to art education led her to found art programs for San Francisco students.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?
Bird Species by Average Mass
Common name | Average mass (kg) | Capable of flight?
Lesser rhea | 19.6 | No
Dalmatian pelican | 11.5 | Yes
Andean condor | 11.3 | Yes
Northern cassowary | 44.0 | No
Most bird species capable of flight weigh under one kilogram (kg), which is unsurprising given the strain that extra body weight places on a flying animal. Yet not every flying bird is so light, as we can see most clearly in the example of the ______
option a: northern cassowary, which has an average mass of 44.0 kg.
option b: Andean condor, which has an average mass below 10 kg.
option c: northern cassowary, which has a higher average mass than the lesser rhea.
option d: Dalmatian pelican, which has an average mass of 11.5 kg.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The Dalmatian pelican is capable of flight yet has an average mass of 11.5 kg, far above one kilogram.
